page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

The underlying AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic accelerations like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In benchmark testing, the ecs.g8a.large demonstrates strong single-core performance, ranking in the top 25% for both stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. However, its multi-core capabilities are more limited, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. This performance profile indicates a strong single-threaded execution capability but a clear tradeoff in parallel processing workloads.

Memory performance is mixed, with write bandwidth for large blocks and PassMark memory scores performing at average levels, while read-only small block memory bandwidth is poor, falling in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also show lower performance, with database operations scoring in the bottom 10% and Redis SET operations in the bottom 25%. Given the lack of local storage and the moderate 2 Gbps network baseline, this instance is appropriate for general-purpose workloads that require strong single-threaded CPU performance but do not demand high multi-core throughput, massive memory bandwidth, or intensive database operations. Suitable applications include lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and single-threaded utility scripts.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor on an x86_64 architecture. Utilizing the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast: the instance delivers strong single-core performance, ranking in the top 25% for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests, but exhibits weak multi-core performance and poor read-only memory bandwidth. Cryptographic and vector extensions like AES and AVX512 are supported. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, the ecs.g8a.large is positioned for entry-level general-purpose workloads, lightweight web serving, and single-threaded tasks, though it is less effective for memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized applications.
